learn.title: Share the multiplier
learn.body: The distributive property says that multiplying a sum is the same as multiplying each part: $a(b+c)=ab+ac$. Test it with numbers: $3(2+5)=3\times 7=21$, and $3\times 2+3\times 5=6+15=21$. Same result.

learn.title: Expand $3(x+4)$
learn.body: Multiply every term inside the brackets by 3.

learn.title: Subtraction and negatives
learn.body: It works with subtraction too: $2(5-y)=10-2y$. When the multiplier is negative, be careful with the signs. $-2(x-3)$ gives $-2x$, and $-2\times(-3)=+6$, so the result is $-2x+6$.

learn.title: Simplify $2(x+3)+4x$
learn.body: Expand first, then combine like terms.
Every term inside gets multiplied, including the last one. $5(2x+1)=10x+5$, not $10x+1$.

questions.explanation: Multiply both terms by 2: $2\times 5=10$ and $2\times y=2y$.

questions.prompt: What is the coefficient of $x$ in $2(x+3)+4x$ after simplifying?
Which is a correct way to compute $4\times 13$?
questions.explanation: Split 13 into $10+3$ and multiply each part: $40+12=52$.

questions.prompt: Simplify $3(x+2)+x$. Put the steps in order.
